approach: Each stage is a Carnot engine, so heat is proportional to temperature; the heat placed in the intermediate reservoir cancels, leaving one engine between T and βT.

steps.text: For the first Carnot stage, write heat as proportional to temperature.
For the second Carnot stage, apply the same proportionality.
The heat Q2 that the first stage deposits in the intermediate reservoir is exactly what the second stage withdraws from it.
steps.equation: net exchange with the αT reservoir = 0
steps.why_this_step: This makes the two stages together equivalent to a single heat engine that takes heat only at T and rejects heat only at βT.

steps.text: Write the overall efficiency of the combined engine.

common_mistakes.text: Ignoring the second stage and reporting only the first stage's efficiency, 1 − α, as the overall efficiency.
Using the original temperature T instead of αT as the hot temperature of the second stage gives Q3 = αβQ1 and an efficiency of 1 − αβ.
